claim: Let \(X\) be nondegenerate with \(0<\mathbb{E}|X|<\infty\), and let \(X^e\) denote the generalized equilibrium transform with density \(F(t)/\mathbb{E}|X|\) for \(t<0\) and \((1-F(t))/\mathbb{E}|X|\) for \(t\ge 0\). Then \(X^e\stackrel{d}{=}X\) if and only if there are \(a>0\) and \(p\in[0,1]\) such that \(X\stackrel{d}{=}SE\), where \(E\) is exponential with mean \(a\), \(S\in\{-1,+1\}\) is independent of \(E\), and \(\mathbb{P}(S=-1)=p\). Equivalently, the fixed-point CDF is \(F(x)=p e^{x/a}\) for \(x<0\) and \(F(x)=1-(1-p)e^{-x/a}\) for \(x\ge0\).
integrity: The theorem is proved analytically in both directions from the published transform definition; no simulation, numerical certificate, or unverified computation is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The result classifies fixed points only; it does not establish convergence of iterates, attraction rates, or exclude nontrivial cycles.
The statement is specific to the Capaldo-Di Crescenzo-Navarro general-support equilibrium transform; other transforms with similar names may have different fixed points.
An equivalent statement under older or different renewal-transform terminology remains a residual literature risk.
title: Fixed points of the generalized equilibrium transform are signed exponentials
